summary: Om Prakash was a scholar of Indology and history and archaeology. He earned his PhD at the University of Delhi under Dasharatha Sharma and studied under Bisheshwar Prasad, later serving at Kirori Mal College and the Delhi School of Economics.

On Shionoya (1878–1962) was a sinologist who studied at Tokyo Imperial University (~1899–1902) and the University of Leipzig (~1906–1909). He held a post at Tokyo Imperial University from around 1920 to 1939.
Orgyen Jikdral Chöying Dorjé was a Tibetan figure who studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé and Thubten Chökyi Dorje.
Orgyen Tendzin Norbu studied under Patrul Rinpoche and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo. He later taught Shenphen Nangwa and Thubten Chökyi Dorje.

Orna Almogi specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied under Khenpo Wangchuk Sonam, David P. Jackson, and Lambert Schmithausen, holding posts at the University of Hamburg, the Nepal-German Manuscript Preservation Project, and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

Osamu Hayashima (b. 1947) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Noritoshi Aramaki. He held professorships at Nagasaki University, Shiga University of Medical Science, and Ryukoku University, and conducted research at the University of Hamburg.
Osamu Izumoji (b. 1948) is a scholar in sinology and other fields. He held academic posts at Kyoto Prefectural University and Ryukoku University.

Osamu Oba (1927–2002) was a scholar of sinology and history/archaeology. After studying at Kansai University (~1950–1953), he taught there (~1958–1997) and later held posts at Kogakkan University (~1997–2002) and the University of the Sacred Heart.

Osamu Takata (1907–1981) worked in history and archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied under Baiei Henmi and served as the head of the art department at the Tokyo National Research Institute for Cultural Properties.

Osborn Bergin (1873–1950) was a linguist who studied under Kuno Meyer and Heinrich Zimmer, attending University College Cork and the University of Freiburg. He later held posts at University College Dublin (~1909–1940) and the Dublin Institute for Advanced Studies.

Oskar von Hinüber (b. 1939) is an Indologist, linguist, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Paul Thieme and earned degrees at Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz. He served as professor at the University of Freiburg (1981–2006) and directed the Nepal Research Centre.

Osmund Bopearachchi (b. 1949) specializes in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at the University of Kelaniya, Panthéon-Sorbonne University, and Paris-Sorbonne University, later holding posts at the CNRS and the University of California, Berkeley.

Osvald Sirén (1879–1966) was a scholar of sinology and art history who studied at the University of Helsinki. He held posts at Stockholm University (1908–1923), the Musée Guimet, and the Nationalmuseum in Stockholm (1926–1945).

Othmar Frank (1770–1840) was a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied at the University of Paris. He served as a professor at the University of Bamberg (~1807–1821), University of Würzburg (1821), and University of Munich (1826).
Otoya Tanaka (1903–1989) was an Indologist who studied at the University of Tokyo under Naoshiro Tsuji. He later served as a professor at Chuo University from around 1952 to 1974.

Otto Blau (1828–1879) was a scholar of linguistics and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He studied under August Friedrich Pott and attended the University of Halle, Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg, and the University of Leipzig.

Otto Fischer (1886–1948) was an art historian and sinologist who completed his habilitation at the University of Göttingen. He served as director of the Staatsgalerie Stuttgart (1920) and Kunstmuseum Basel (1927), and taught at the University of Basel (~1927–1937).

Otto Franke (1863–1946) was a sinologist and Indologist who studied under Wilhelm Grube and at the universities of Freiburg and Göttingen. He held chairs at the Hamburgisches Kolonialinstitut/University of Hamburg (from 1910) and Humboldt University of Berlin (1923–1931).

Otto Höfler (1901–1987) was a linguist and religious studies scholar who studied under Rudolf Much at the University of Vienna. He held professorships at Kiel University (1935), the University of Munich (1938–1945; 1954), and the University of Vienna (1957–1971).
Otto Jahn (1813–1869) was an archaeologist and classicist who studied at Kiel, Leipzig, and Berlin. He held academic posts at the universities of Greifswald, Kiel, Leipzig, and Bonn.
